name: Jakub Wiśniewski
source: Poznań University of Technology, CS program 2012
context: CTO of our startup. We've been building together since the dorm room days. Mass of contradictions — mass of patience, zero patience for bad UI. Runs ultramarathons, uses running metaphors for everything. Wife Ola is a pediatrician.
last_interaction_summary: Slack thread at 1am debating whether to hire a senior backend dev or two juniors.
notes: Jakub's birthday is June 12. Ola is pregnant — due late July. They don't want people to know yet, he told me in confidence.

name: Ola Wiśniewska
context: Pediatrician at a clinic in Mokotów. Calm, warm, somehow tolerates both of us. We do a yearly couples dinner with her and Jakub, me and Tomek.
last_interaction_summary: She texted me a photo of a ridiculously tiny pair of sneakers she bought.

name: Tomek Lis
source: met at a friend's birthday party, 2021
context: Works as a documentary filmmaker, currently editing a piece on Polish diaspora communities in Iceland. Very different world from startups — keeps me grounded. Hates networking events but comes to the important ones.
last_interaction_summary: Morning coffee — he asked me if I'm sleeping enough. I'm not.
notes: Tomek's mom's name is Grażyna, lives in Lublin. He's sensitive about people treating his work as a hobby. Remember to actually watch the rough cut he sent me last week — I keep saying I will.

name: Agnieszka Kowalczyk
context: Agnieszka teaches math at a liceum in Wrocław. Divorced last year, has two kids: Zuzia (9) and Michał (6). She worries about me constantly. We talk on the phone most Sundays.
last_interaction_summary: Sunday call — she's thinking about moving to Warsaw for a fresh start. Wants to talk more about it next week.
notes: Zuzia's birthday is May 3. I promised Agnieszka I'd help her look at apartments in Ursynów if she decides to move. Haven't started looking yet.

name: Paweł Zieliński
context: Now angel investor, did 12 deals last year. Very well connected in Polish tech. Blunt feedback style — if he says it's good, it's good. Divorced, two teenage sons. Collects vinyl records.
last_interaction_summary: Quick Slack back-and-forth about a vinyl reissue he just tracked down — he sent three voice notes.
notes: Paweł said he'd intro me to Beata Nowak at Market One Capital — I need to follow up and ask if he's sent the email yet. He also mentioned he's thinking about doing a podcast, asked if I knew anyone in audio production.

name: Magda Kamińska
context: Left tech entirely, now runs a small ceramics studio in Kazimierz Dolny. We've stayed close despite completely different paths. She's the person I call when everything feels like too much.
last_interaction_summary: Quick evening call — she sent me a photo of a new glaze she's testing, made me laugh.
notes: Magda's studio anniversary is in June — she's doing an exhibition. I said I'd come. Need to block the weekend.

name: Anna Kwiatkowska
context: Partner at Movens Capital, focuses on B2B SaaS. Ex-McKinsey, then product at DocPlanner. Very data-driven, asks hard questions about unit economics. Has a dry sense of humor once you get past the formality.
last_interaction_summary: Video call — she wants updated MRR numbers and a customer cohort analysis before their Monday IC meeting. Said she's "cautiously optimistic."
notes: URGENT: I need to send her the cohort analysis by end of day Thursday. She also asked about our churn rate by segment — I said I'd break it out. Don't drop this.

name: Michał Dąbrowski
context: Former CTO at Booksy, now full-time angel. Writes checks quickly, doesn't need a lot of hand-holding. Interested in developer tools. Has a golden retriever named Bigos.
last_interaction_summary: He committed 50k to the round via email. Quick and clean.
notes: Check went through. Need to send him the SAFE docs — told him I'd send by Friday last week and I still haven't.

name: Beata Nowak
source: warm intro pending from Paweł Zieliński
context: Managing Partner at Market One Capital. Supposedly very founder-friendly, loves repeat founders. Was early in Packhelp and Zowie. I haven't actually met her yet.
last_interaction_summary: Paweł forwarded my LinkedIn profile to her with a note — she viewed it but hasn't responded yet.
notes: Paweł was supposed to intro me. I should check if he did — it's been two weeks.

name: Katarzyna Sikora
source: met at her office hours at Reaktor, 2025
context: Principal at Inovo. Young, sharp, from Kraków. Studied at LSE. Particularly interested in AI infrastructure. Tends to ask very specific technical questions.
last_interaction_summary: In-person meeting at their office. Good conversation but she pushed back on our positioning — thinks we're "too horizontal." Said she'd discuss with the partnership.
notes: She mentioned they're also looking at a competitor — wouldn't say who. I should send her the case study from the FinBridge pilot to show vertical depth.

name: Piotr Grabowski
context: Engineering leader, now VP Eng at Packhelp. Deep infrastructure knowledge. Advises us informally on architecture decisions. Speaks slowly, thinks carefully.
last_interaction_summary: Lunch at Bibenda. Discussed our database migration plan. He flagged a potential issue with our sharding approach, sent me a link afterward that I haven't read yet.
notes: He's been advising us for free for months. I should formalize this — equity or at least a proper advisor agreement. Feels awkward to bring up.

name: Marek Jankowski
context: Head of Product at FinBridge, a fintech doing SME lending. They have exactly the pain point we solve. Mid-40s, pragmatic, not easily impressed.
last_interaction_summary: Demo call went well. He wants to run a 4-week pilot starting May. Needs a proposal doc and data security questionnaire from us.
notes: TODO: Send him the pilot proposal and security questionnaire. His compliance team needs it before they can sign anything. Also need to CC their DPO, whose name I forgot to write down.

name: Dorota Majewska
source: met at Product Hunt launch, commented on our post
context: CPO at PeopleForce (HR platform, Kyiv/Warsaw). Energetic, talks fast. Very active on Twitter. Their team is 100+, might be a great mid-market case study.
last_interaction_summary: Twitter DM exchange. She's interested in a pilot but said Q2 is insane for them — suggested reconnecting in June.
notes: Reconnect in June. She also asked if we integrate with Slack — we don't yet, but it's on the roadmap.

name: Filip Wójcik
context: Senior backend engineer, currently at Netguru. 7 years of experience, strong in Go. Looking to join an early-stage startup. Seems motivated by ownership, not just comp.
last_interaction_summary: Technical interview — Jakub liked him a lot. We're deciding between him and one other candidate.
notes: Good culture fit. Salary expectation is 28k PLN net, which is at the top of our range. Jakub thinks he's worth it.

name: Hanna Lewandowska
context: Now Head of Design at Docplanner. We overlapped for two years, stayed loosely in touch. She's incredible at user research — I've thought about asking her to moonlight for us.
last_interaction_summary: Bumped into her at a meetup in Warsaw. Quick catch-up. She mentioned she's burned out and thinking about taking a sabbatical.
notes: She knows Anna Kwiatkowska from Docplanner days — could be useful context but also could be awkward since Anna is evaluating our round.

name: Klaus Weber
context: Partner at Cherry Ventures. Covers CEE from Berlin. Tall, very German-efficient in meetings. Interested in PLG B2B SaaS. Did Vantage and Maze.
last_interaction_summary: Video call. He liked the product but said we're too early for Cherry — wants to see us again at Series A. Offered to intro us to a few angels in Berlin.
notes: He mentioned Tobias Schreier as a potential angel — said he'd intro if I wanted. I said yes but never followed up.

name: Tobias Schreier
context: CTO at a fintech in Berlin (can't remember the name). Apparently writes 25-50k angel checks in dev tools. I don't know him yet.
last_interaction_summary: Klaus sent a brief email intro connecting us — I replied but Tobias hasn't responded.
notes: Klaus was going to intro me. Should follow up with Klaus.

name: Joanna Nowicka
context: Partner at Wardyński & Partners, specializes in VC/startup law. Handles our SAFE agreements and will do the seed round docs. Crisp, efficient, doesn't waste words.
last_interaction_summary: Email exchange about the SAFE template for Michał's investment. She sent a redline I need to review.
notes: She quoted 15k PLN for the full round documentation. Need to confirm and sign engagement letter.

name: Łukasz Borkowski
context: Works at Google Zurich as a senior SWE. We were close in uni but drifted apart. He's into climbing and mechanical keyboards. Married to someone named Petra, no kids.
last_interaction_summary: He visited Warsaw, we grabbed beers. Fun night but felt like we were catching up out of obligation more than genuine connection.

name: Maria Fernandez
context: Product manager, Spanish, based in Warsaw for 3 years. Previously at Brainly. Strong analytical background, speaks fluent Polish. Interested in early-stage roles.
last_interaction_summary: Coffee meeting. Sharp, asked great questions about our ICP. She's exploring options but not in a rush — has a 3-month notice period.
notes: She's also talking to Productboard. We should move fast if we want her. I told her I'd get back to her within two weeks — it's been six.

name: Szymon Czajka
source: worked together at Allegro, overlapped with Paweł Zieliński
context: Now co-founder of a logistics startup (LoadMe). We were on the same team at Allegro under Paweł. Competitive but in a mostly healthy way. His startup is about a year ahead of ours in fundraising.
last_interaction_summary: Ran into him at a KPT event. Tried to compare notes on fundraising but he was weirdly cagey — felt like he didn't want to share info anymore.
notes: Used to be close. Since we're both fundraising, there's a weird competitive energy. He's also talking to Inovo — wonder if his company is the competitor Katarzyna mentioned.

name: Ewa Pietrzak
context: Runs a small accounting firm specializing in startups and R&D tax credits. Reliable, responsive, not the cheapest but worth it.
last_interaction_summary: Monthly financials review call. Everything clean. She flagged we should start thinking about IP Box.

name: Adam Nowicki
source: met at MIT Enterprise Forum Poland, 2025
context: Associate at Cogito Capital, their new early-stage fund. Young, eager, seems to have less decision-making power than he lets on. Background in data science.
last_interaction_summary: He asked for a follow-up call after I pitched at the forum. Enthusiastic but vague on timeline. Kept saying he needs to "align with the team."

name: Natalia Wróbel
source: LinkedIn, she pitched me her services, 2025
context: Does PR for startups — worked with Symmetrical and Tidio. Good at getting press in Puls Biznesu and Rzeczpospolita. Based in Gdańsk.
last_interaction_summary: She sent a proposal for a 3-month PR retainer. 8k PLN/month. I said I'd think about it.

name: James Chen
source: met at API World 2024, San Francisco
context: Developer Relations lead at Segment. We discussed a potential integration. American-Chinese, lives in SF, super energetic, lots of ideas. Wore a very memorable neon green jacket.
last_interaction_summary: Exchanged a few emails after the conference. He was excited initially but then went quiet. Might have changed roles.
notes: Last email from him went unanswered — mine, not his. I owe him a reply from August.

name: Zofia Adamczyk
context: QA engineer turned engineering manager at Ocado Technology. Meticulous, very organized. We weren't close at STX but reconnected when she moved to Warsaw.
last_interaction_summary: Coffee. She's frustrated at Ocado — politics, slow pace. Hinted she might be open to something new.

name: Rafael Santos
context: Partner at Indico Capital, Lisbon. Covers B2B SaaS across Europe. Brazilian-Portuguese, very warm personality. Did early rounds in Amplemarket and Codacy.
last_interaction_summary: Good meeting at Web Summit. He asked me to send our deck. I did, he said he'd review after the holidays.

name: Mateusz Krawczyk
relationship: friend of a friend, now advisor candidate
source: introduced by Magda Kamińska at her birthday party, 2023
context: Serial entrepreneur, sold his e-commerce company to Grupa Pracuj in 2021. Now does advisory work and invests casually. Charismatic, tells great stories, sometimes hard to pin down on specifics.
last_interaction_summary: He offered to help with go-to-market strategy. We had one call, it was useful, then scheduling fell apart.
notes: He said he'd review our pricing model but we never scheduled the follow-up. My fault — I got swamped.

name: Iga Stankiewicz
source: Dribbble, I reached out to her, 2024
context: Brand and UI designer, did our logo and initial design system. Based in Łódź. Very talented, a bit unreliable with timelines. Has a cat named Pixel.
last_interaction_summary: She finished the investor deck design. Great work, delivered 4 days late as usual.
notes: Owes me final invoice for the deck work. I think it was around 3500 PLN.

name: Wojciech Mazur
source: Poznań University of Technology, thesis advisor
context: Professor of distributed systems. Supervised both me and Jakub. Still at the university, nearing retirement. Dry humor, always wearing a corduroy jacket.
last_interaction_summary: He emailed asking if we'd give a guest lecture to his students about startup engineering. I said yes but we never set a date.
notes: I should schedule that lecture — I said yes months ago. He's probably too polite to ask again.

name: Elena Voronova
context: Data scientist, Ukrainian, moved to Warsaw in 2022. PhD in NLP from KPI Kyiv. Currently at Samsung R&D. Very sharp, quiet until she has something important to say.
last_interaction_summary: Informational coffee. She's interested in joining an AI startup but wants to understand the product deeply first. I gave her access to our sandbox.
notes: She asked really good questions about our model architecture. Follow up in two weeks — she said she'd play with the sandbox and come back with thoughts.

name: Bartosz Kaczmarek
context: Co-founder of a food-tech startup that folded in 2023. Now does product consulting. Funny, self-deprecating about the failure. We grab beers every few months.
last_interaction_summary: Beers at Kufle i Kapsle. He's thinking about starting something new in climate tech. Wanted to brainstorm. Good conversation.

name: Alicja Marczak
context: Director of Digital Transformation at PZU (insurance). Big corporate energy but genuinely trying to innovate. Controls a decent budget.
last_interaction_summary: Intro call. She described their pain points — actually a great fit for us. But PZU procurement is a nightmare, 6-month cycles minimum.
notes: She said to reach out again in Q3 when their new budget cycle starts. Put a reminder.

name: Lars Eriksson
source: met at a dinner hosted by Klaus Weber in Berlin, 2024
context: VP of Sales at Pleo (Copenhagen). Knows the European B2B SaaS playbook cold. Swedish, very structured thinker. Married to a partner at Northzone.
last_interaction_summary: Good dinner conversation. He gave me advice on pricing for SMB vs. mid-market. Said to reach out if I ever need Nordics intros.
notes: His wife is at Northzone — could potentially be a path to a conversation there for Series A. Don't want to be transactional about it though.

name: Karolina Duda
context: Now runs marketing at Brand24. We were friendly but not close. She's become very active on LinkedIn — posts every day, growing audience.
last_interaction_summary: She commented on my LinkedIn post about our product launch. I replied but we didn't take it further.

name: Artur Szymański
context: Retired pharma exec, does angel investing as a hobby. Old-school — prefers printed decks and face-to-face meetings. Surprisingly tech-savvy for his age.
last_interaction_summary: Met at Cosmo for coffee. He wants to invest 100k but has a lot of questions about the cap table. Doesn't understand SAFEs well.
notes: Joanna Nowicka offered to explain the SAFE structure to him directly. I should connect them.

name: Weronika Bak
context: Left tech for medicine — now a resident in radiology at a hospital in Kraków. We were in the same study group. She brings a completely outside perspective when I vent about startup stuff.
last_interaction_summary: She visited Warsaw for a conference. Quick dinner. She looked exhausted — residency is brutal.
notes: Her wedding is in September 2026, in Kraków. Save the date — it's a Saturday.

name: Damian Ostrowski
context: Owns the building where we have our office space in Mokotów. Retired engineer, a bit grumpy, but fair. Fixes things quickly when asked.
last_interaction_summary: Lease renewal discussion. He wants to raise rent by 12%. I pushed back, settled on 8%.
notes: Lease renewed through end of 2026. He mentioned he might sell the building next year — could mean we need to move.

name: Sophie Laurent
source: met at Station F event, Paris, 2024
context: Co-founder of a French startup doing AI-powered contract analysis. Potential integration partner. Very polished, MBA from INSEAD. Based in Paris.
last_interaction_summary: We had a video call about a potential co-marketing arrangement. It fizzled — neither of us followed through.

name: Krzysztof Wiater
context: Co-founder of an analytics tool for SaaS companies. Not a direct competitor but close enough that investors sometimes lump us together. Good guy, very transparent about his numbers.
last_interaction_summary: He DM'd me asking if I'd heard anything about Inovo's new fund. I shared what I knew. Felt like mutual intel-gathering.

name: Julia Kwiecień
source: she reached out for a comment, 2024
context: Tech journalist at Spider's Web. Covers Polish startups and VC. Fair, does her homework. Good to stay on her radar.
last_interaction_summary: She interviewed me for a piece on Polish SaaS companies raising abroad. Article was balanced, good coverage.

name: Oliwia Jankowska
source: introduced by Agnieszka at a family gathering, 2024
context: Runs a small recruitment agency in Wrocław. 15 employees. Classic SMB pain points — uses spreadsheets for everything. Could be an early adopter.
last_interaction_summary: She tried our free trial. Said she liked it but didn't convert. Feedback: onboarding was confusing.

name: Marcus Thompson
source: met at API World 2024, San Francisco
context: Developer advocate at Twilio. We bonded over being non-Americans at an American conference. From London originally. Knows the API ecosystem deeply.
last_interaction_summary: We grabbed tacos after the conference. Fun guy, lots of energy. Exchanged numbers but haven't talked since.

name: Dominik Szulc
context: Works in commercial real estate. Not in tech at all but surprisingly well-connected in Warsaw business circles. We see each other at Jakub and Ola's dinner parties.
last_interaction_summary: Christmas dinner at Jakub and Ola's. He told a hilarious story about a deal gone wrong. Good vibes.
notes: He once offered to help us find cheaper office space. Might be worth taking him up on that if Damian sells the building.

name: Renata Kaczor
context: Runs an impact-focused micro VC in Warsaw. Interested in tech-for-good angles. Former UNDP, very mission-driven. We disagree on whether profit-first or impact-first is the right framing, but the conversations are stimulating.
last_interaction_summary: She challenged me on our DEI hiring practices at a panel afterparty. Uncomfortable but fair points.

name: Henrik Olsen
context: Founded a Nordic HR-tech SaaS, about 2 years ahead of us in stage. Very generous with his time. We compared notes on European expansion and pricing.
last_interaction_summary: He sent me a Loom video breaking down his pricing page evolution. Incredibly generous — unsolicited.
notes: He uses the same law firm as Lars Eriksson. Small world. Should reconnect and update him on our progress.

name: Grzegorz Wilk
context: Retired, used to work in banking. Watches our packages. We chat in the stairwell. He's lonely since his wife passed — sometimes talks for too long but I don't have the heart to cut him off.
last_interaction_summary: Ran into him by the mailboxes. He asked about my work — I tried to explain SaaS, he nodded politely.
notes: His daughter works at mBank in some senior role. He's mentioned it three times. Probably wants me to ask for an intro.

name: Martyna Głowacka
source: met at Google for Startups accelerator, 2023
context: Founded a quantum computing startup. Brilliant, slightly intimidating. PhD in physics. We were in the same GFS cohort.
last_interaction_summary: She raised a 2M EUR seed from Speedinvest. Congratulated her on LinkedIn, she replied warmly.

name: Piotr Szczepanik
source: met through Tomek, at a screening, 2023
context: Documentary editor, works with Tomek occasionally. Thoughtful, quiet. We've talked about how storytelling applies to pitching — actually insightful.
last_interaction_summary: Tomek's screening event. Piotr and I had a long conversation about narrative structure in pitch decks. He made me rethink our story arc.

name: Aneta Michalak
source: sat next to her at a dinner hosted by Artur Szymański, 2025
context: Director at PKO BP's innovation lab. They run a corporate accelerator and are looking for B2B SaaS tools to pilot internally. Polished, corporate, but genuinely curious.
last_interaction_summary: She emailed me asking for a one-pager about our product for her team's review. I said I'd send it Monday.
notes: I told her I'd send the one-pager on Monday. That was three Mondays ago.
